answer: Each agent earns a reputation token minted in a marble‑hard ledger only after it successfully forges a proof of work that includes a saffron‑colored nonce, binding the token to a unique computational fingerprint. The network then applies quadratic weighting, so the influence of any identity grows with the square of its reputation, making a bundle of low‑cost Sybil accounts count far less than one well‑established node. An attacker must therefore invest computational power proportional to the square of the desired influence, quickly exceeding realistic cost thresholds.
